statement: Domaine Labet is a family wine estate based in Rotalier in the southern Jura / Sud-Revermont; the Jura interprofessional profile documents 13.5 hectares across 45 parcels in four communes.
The Jura interprofessional profile identifies Alain, Julien, Charline and Romain Labet among the family vignerons of Domaine Labet.
The official Jura profile describes Domaine Labet's ouillé white-wine practice as élevage on lees in older oak barrels topped weekly to prevent oxidation and development of a yeast veil.
Domaine Labet's Fleur de Savagnin is documented as a Savagnin blend assembled from multiple Lias-marl parcels rather than a single vineyard wine; the listed plantings span multiple years and sites.

The Jura interprofessional profile describes La Cuvée du Hasard as Chardonnay from vines older than 60 years, blended from different Lias-marl terroirs and aged sous voile in old 228-litre pièces for 36 to 48 months.

resolution_needed: No fit source verified fortification for Chardonnay du Hasard; reopen only if producer or comparably fit technical evidence documents it.
statement: The research-handoff assertion that Domaine Labet Chardonnay du Hasard is fortified to approximately 15% alcohol before flor development is rejected: the official Jura description documents extended sous-voile élevage but does not document fortification.

resolution_needed: Avoid any estate-wide claim that Labet whites prevent malolactic fermentation; scope future malolactic claims to a wine and vintage.
statement: The research-handoff generalization that Domaine Labet avoids malolactic fermentation in white wines is rejected; Revue du Vin de France documents sulfur additions after malolactic fermentation in its account of the estate's white-wine work.

For the 2022 La Bardette Chardonnay, specialist retail/importer notes describe a 0.5-hectare west-facing La Bardette parcel planted in 1947 and more than 30 months of aging in used 228-litre barrels; the estate's broader La Bardette holdings include plantings of other ages, so this detail is scoped to the 2022 single-parcel bottling.
Vins Pepe Raventós is the small personal wine project in which Pepe Raventós makes parcel-based natural wines at the Mas del Serral garage; the producer describes this work as beginning in 2014.

The 2022 Bastard Negre de les Terrasses del Serral is documented as 100% Bastard Negre from a west-side parcel planted in 1974 on shallow calcareous clay-loam soil, with spontaneous fermentation in three open 225-litre casks and one qvevri.
Spain's official commercial vine-variety register lists Morrastel among the recognized synonyms of Graciano.

resolution_needed: A primary scientific genetics source directly linking the estate's Bastard Negre accession to Graciano would upgrade this from provisional to supported biological identity.
statement: Raventós reports that 2012 DNA analysis identified its Bastard Negre planting as Morastell; because the Spanish official register recognizes Morrastel as a synonym of Graciano, CARTA provisionally treats Bastard Negre as a local estate/Penedès name attached to the Graciano identity rather than creating a separate grape entity.
Soleras del Pacífico is Jake Neustadt's project, begun from the opportunity in 2017 to work with old Palomino vines at Evangelho Vineyard while he was working as a Bedrock Wine Co. viticulturist.

Evangelho Vineyard in Contra Costa County was planted in the 1890s on deep sandy soils; Soleras del Pacífico documents just over 100 Palomino vines there, while Bedrock identifies itself as the vineyard owner and farmer.

The Flor of Evangelho is documented as a single-vineyard Palomino Fino wine in a fino-style solera established in 2017: native barrel fermentation is followed by light spring fortification to favor flor, fractional blending through a four-level solera, maturation under flor and unfiltered bottling.

Eruptio is documented by Abegoaria and contemporaneous Portuguese launch reporting as a wine project led by winemaker Bernardo Cabral in partnership with Abegoaria, with production associated with Adega do Pico.

resolution_needed: Do not attribute Eruptio to António Maçanita unless new first-party or legal evidence supersedes the Abegoaria/Cabral record.
statement: The retailer assertion that Eruptio was conceived by António Maçanita is rejected for CARTA authority because it conflicts with specific first-party Abegoaria attribution and contemporaneous Portuguese launch reporting naming Bernardo Cabral and Abegoaria.
Abegoaria's 2020 product page identifies Eruptio Arinto dos Açores as a Pico D.O. wine made from Arinto dos Açores, fermented in French oak and aged six months on fine lees.

Portugal's official vine-variety list records Arinto dos Açores as a distinct variety entry with Terrantez da Terceira as a recognized synonym; it separately records mainland Arinto with Pedernã as its recognized synonym.

Weingut Keller is a Rheinhessen, Germany estate based in Flörsheim-Dalsheim and associated with Klaus-Peter Keller; the reconciliation uses the producer identity only to anchor the verified Limestone and RR wines.

The trade portfolio distinguishes Keller Riesling limestone and Keller Riesling Kabinett limestone as separate wines, while also listing a separate Rheinhessen Riesling Trocken; CARTA therefore keeps the two Limestone wines as distinct durable identities rather than treating dry/off-dry expressions as one wine.

resolution_needed: Do not rename the base Limestone identity as 'Limestone trocken' without wine- and vintage-specific evidence; the verified portfolio separates Riesling Trocken from Riesling limestone.
statement: The research-handoff simplification that Keller's base Riesling Limestone is the dry/trocken counterpart to Limestone Kabinett is rejected: the verified portfolio lists Riesling Trocken, Riesling limestone and Riesling Kabinett limestone as separate entries.
Vom Boden describes Keller Riesling RR as normally sourced from a rare red-soil parcel within Westhofener Kirchspiel and as a feinherb wine whose RR label denotes Riesling from Red soil.

For the 2022 vintage, vom Boden reports that Keller RR included top casks from Abtserde and Morstein in addition to its normal Kirchspiel red-soil basis because those casks stopped short of dry; this is a vintage-scoped sourcing variation within the continuing RR identity.
Cathy Corison founded Corison Winery and began making Cabernet Sauvignon under her own name in 1987.

Corison's Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon is the winery's continuing Cabernet identity begun in 1987 and sourced from three benchland vineyards between Rutherford and St. Helena; it remains distinct from the Kronos and Sunbasket single-vineyard wines.

Corison documents Kronos Vineyard as planted in 1971 on St. George rootstock and purchased by Cathy Corison and William Martin in 1995; it is the source of the distinct Kronos Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon.

Corison purchased Sunbasket Vineyard in 2015 after sourcing fruit from the site for more than 25 years; Sunbasket Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon is represented as a distinct single-vineyard wine identity.
TTB lists St. Helena as an established California American Viticultural Area with an establishment date of September 11, 1995.
